question: The authority to extend or approve credit is granted to individual credit officer based on their grades, portfolonand length of stay in the organization.

question: In underwriting and distribution activities, in the event of a commitment to purchase a security or other debt instrument from an issuer or seller, there is a risk of inability to sell instrument within a predetermined distribution period to an investor or purchaser.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 3.5.2 Issuer Risk) In underwriting and distribution activities, in the event of a commitment to purchase a security or other debt instrument from an issuer or seller, there is a risk of inability to sell the instrument within a predetermined distribution period to an investor or purchaser. In this event, direct lending risk and unintended price risk is created. This risk is sometimes also described as issuer risk.

question: Price risk is the risk that market conditions may change for an individual instrument or for all securities of the same general class.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 3.5.8 Price Risk) Price risk is the risk that market conditions may change for an individual instrument or for all securities of the same general class. For example, a change in the level of interest rates affects the price of all interest rate sensitive instruments. Price risk is not to be confused with issuer risk, which describes price changes attributable to real and perceives changes in the quality of a particular issuer and instrument.

question: Fiduciary risk occurs when the bank is charge with the responsibilities of acting as a trustee for third parties i.e. if a trust agreement is not in place clearly outlining the duties and responsibilities of the bank and when the bank may be exposed to potential or real conflict of interest
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 3.5.10 Fiduciary Risk) Fiduciary risk occurs when the bank is charged with the responsibility of acting as a trustee for third parties.

question: Is it right to state that in the absence of approved credit programs, transaction for individual customers or customer relationships will be treated as individual/business credit?
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 6.2.9.2 Individual / Business Credit) In the absence of approved credit programs, transactions for individual customers or customer relationships will be treated as individual/business credits. With this approach, credit is approved using the approval process as defined in the risk management policies to the bank. This shall entail detailed and comprehensive evaluation of the proposed transaction in the context of existing exposures to a particular customer. Credit approval may be for a single, simple product or for a series of large complex transactions.

question: Risk rating limits is the only mechanism to control the Bank’s portfolio of credit exposures.
discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 5.3.5 Risk Rating Limits) Access Bank will use Risk Rating Limits as the primary mechanism not the only mechanism to control its portfolio of credit exposures.

question: For purposes of applying Risk rating limits, which of the following is true; the obligor risk rating that is used must be:

options.A: For corporations, the obligor risk rating of the present company
options.B: For bank syndicated loans, the risk rating of the bank
options.C: For other entities, the risk rating as determined in accordance with the Risk Rating Policy.

discussion: Selected Answer: D. (Section 5.3.5.1 Measuring Exposure against Risk Rating Limits) "The Risk Rating Limit process outlined below applies to exposure at the overall relationship level. For the purposes of applying Risk Rating Limits, the obligor risk rating that is used must be: • For corporations, the obligor risk rating of the parent company. • For banks, the risk rating of the lead bank. • For other entity types, the risk rating as determined in accordance Access Bank’s Risk Rating Policy. Exposure against Risk Rating Limits is measured as the Outstanding’s and Unused Commitments (“OSUC”) to a given relationship. • OSUC is the sum of all Outstandings (including Direct and Contingent Exposure) against Total Facilities, as well as the unused portion of any Committed Facility included in Total Facilities. • OSUC does not include settlement and clearing exposure, or the Underwritten Position of a credit underwriting transaction unless the position becomes aged beyond the Extension Period. • For purposes of measuring exposure against Risk Rating Limit tenor buckets, contractual principal repayments may be taken into consideration.

question: A proposal or marketing letter does not require credit approval if it does not obligate the bank in any way.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 5.3.6 Establish Total Facilities) A proposal or marketing letter does not require credit approval if it expressly disclaims any commitment or any undertaking to provide a commitment or other services and does not obligate Access Bank in any way.

question: What components should each Portfolio Management Process incorporate?

question: All credit requests that are above the limit of the Regional MD must be approved at the next higher appropriate level-GDMD/GMD/MCC/BCC/BOARD.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 6.2.10.4.1 Determine the Required Approvals) Credit requests that are above the limit of the Regional MDs will be approved at the next higher appropriate level MD / MCC / BCC / Board.

question: An offer letter is a commitment by the bank to lend to customers once the terms and conditions contained in the letter have been satisfied.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 6.2.15 Offer Letters) An Offer Letter is a commitment by the Bank to lend to a customer once the terms and conditions contained in the letter have been satisfied.

question: Revolving credits are short term facilities with predefined cycles that relate to the customer’s objectives and plans.
discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 3.6.2 Revolving Credits) Revolving credits are short term/tenured facilities with predefined cycles that relate to the customer’s business/trading cycle.

question: The Forced Sale Value of the goods financed ought to be adequate to cover the bank’s exposure at the commencement of the facility.
discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 3.6.5 Warehouse Financing) The forced sale value of the goods must be adequate to cover the bank’s exposure at all times.

question: All independent local policies of the country office must be endorsed by group Office Credit Risk Management and approved by the GMD
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 2.6 Establishment of Risk Management Policies) The countries may also originate independent local policies i.e. policies for issues not specifically addressed in Head Office policies. In addition to approval by the Head of Credit Risk Management at the country level and MD for the relevant country, such policies must be endorsed by Credit Risk Management, Group Office and approved by the MD.

question: Whose responsibility is it to ensure that the provisions of the CPG remain relevant and adequate?

options.E: All personnel who are involved in the credit process

discussion: Selected Answer: E. (Section 2.8 Guidelines for Changing and Approving Policy Changes) All Access Bank personnel who are involved in the credit process and apply these guidelines on a continual basis shall be responsible for ensuring that the provisions remain relevant and adequate to address the changing needs of the environment, as well as support the achievement of the bank’s business goals and objectives.
community_answer: E. All personnel who are involved in the credit process

question: The Board of Trustees will approve all changes to the CPG
discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 4.2.1.2 Board Credit Committee) The Board Credit committee shall under delegated authority be responsible for the following: Approve changes to credit policy guidelines on the recommendation of the Management Credit Committee (MCC) .

question: As a Banker, you must make a conscious effort to continuously strengthen your integrity.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 10.6.8 Appraisal Procedure and Lending Process) Access Bank officers (or appointed consultants where applicable) are fully responsible to the Bank and to no other institution or agency in carrying out their duties. They must therefore apply themselves with all sense of seriousness, professionalism and integrity.

question: A key principle of credit policy is that the Bank will always comply with all Government regulations.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 5.3.3.1 Regulatory Considerations) Access Bank Plc is subject to laws and regulations issued by the Central Bank of Nigeria, or other agencies of the Federal Republic of Nigeria that are established for the regulation of financial institutions.

question: If we break regulations and this information reaches the market, our reputation will be diminished.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 10.7.5.2) Compliance risk can lead to a diminished reputation.

question: A letter of credit (LC) is a conditional written undertaking issued by a bank to an exporter (beneficiary) at the request of an importer (applicant) to effect payment for a stated amount against a presentation of document that complies with the terms of the LC.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 3.6.14 Letter of Credit) A letter of credit (LC) is a conditional written undertaking issued by a bank to an exporter (beneficiary) at the request of an importer (applicant) to effect payment for a stated amount against a presentation of document that complies with the terms of the LC.

question: Access Bank can buy or fund the purchase of a capital asset at a client’s request and hire or lease it to them at an agreed rental.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 3.6.4 Lease Facilities) A lease facility exists where Access Bank acquires or funds the acquisition of capital assets at a client’s request and then hires or leases the asset back to the client for an agreed periodic rental.

question: The title of a financed capital asset resides with the client until the last instalment is paid and the client exercises its option to purchase the asset at the pre-determined price stated in the lease agreement.
discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 3.6.4 Lease Facilities) Title to the asset remains with the bank until when fully repaid and the client exercises the option to purchase the asset for a predetermined price.

question: What is a key responsibility of the relationship manager in facility performance monitoring?

options.B: Monitor performance of credit facilities and confirming adherence to credit terms and conditions on an ongoing basis.

discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 6.3.14 Facility Performance Monitoring) The relationship manager with responsibility for each customer relationship shall on an ongoing basis monitor the performance of individual credit facilities and confirm adherence to credit terms and conditions.
community_answer: B. Monitor performance of credit facilities and confirming adherence to credit terms and conditions on an ongoing basis.

question: Why are financial and non-financial covenants mandated for credit facilities?

options.A: To increase the complexity of loan agreements
options.B: To facilitate monitoring and control activities efficiently
options.D: To eliminate any form of analysis on obligors' performance.

discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 6.3.15 Standard Financial and Non-Financial Covenants) Financial and Non-Financial Covenants are mandated in order to monitor the financial and overall performance of the obligors with regard to the credit facilities granted.
community_answer: B. To facilitate monitoring and control activities efficiently

question: How often are reports generated by Credit Risk Management Groups regarding adherence to financial and non-financial covenants?
discussion: Selected Answer: C. (Section 6.3.15.3 Monitoring of Adherence to Financial and Non-Financial Covenants) Credit Risk Management Groups will generate reports on a monthly basis, on the adherence to the financial and non-financial covenants at facility and borrower level.

question: The bank-wide credit portfolio is reviewed on a monthly basis in compliance with Prudential Guidelines.
discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 6.4.20 Exposure Quality Classifications) The bank wide credit portfolio will be reviewed on a quarterly basis in compliance with Prudential Guidelines.

question: A restructured facility can be further restructured without any improvement in the obligor's performance.
discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 6.5.4 Restructuring of Credit Facilities) A restructured facility cannot be further restructured unless definite improvement has been recorded.

question: When is a credit facility considered performing?

options.A: When payments of interest are up-to-date
options.B: When payments of principal are up-to-date
options.D: When both principal and interest payments are up-to-date

discussion: Selected Answer: D. (Section 6.4.21 Definition of Default) A credit facility is deemed to be performing if payments of both principal and interest are up-to-date in accordance with the agreed terms.
community_answer: D. When both principal and interest payments are up-to-date

question: In what circumstances is a credit facility deemed non-performing?

options.A: If interest is due for 90 days or more
options.B: If principal is due for 90 days or more
options.C: If both interest and principal are due for 90 days or more

discussion: Selected Answer: D. (Section 6.4.21 Definition of Default) A credit facility will be deemed as non-performing when any of the following conditions exists: • interest or principal is due and unpaid for 90 days or more • interest payments equal to 90 days’ interest or more have been capitalized, rescheduled or rolled over into a new loan (except where facilities have been reclassifieD) .

question: What is an Offer Letter in the context of credit facilities from the bank?

options.B: A legal commitment by the customer
options.C: An invitation to apply for a loan.
options.D: A commitment by the bank to lend once certain conditions are met

discussion: Selected Answer: D. (Section 6.2.15 Offer Letters) An Offer Letter is a commitment by the Bank to lend to a customer once the terms and conditions contained in the letter have been satisfied.
community_answer: D. A commitment by the bank to lend once certain conditions are met

question: The Legal Department must review and initial each page of an Offer Letter that deviates from the standard format.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 6.2.15 Offer Letters) Any Offer Letter that deviates from the standard format must be reviewed by an officer in Legal Department, and such review will be evidenced by the initial of the officer on each page of the offer letter.

question: The frequency of customer visits is solely based on the Chief Risk Officer's discretion.
discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 6.6.1 Customer Meetings and Call Reports) The frequency of these visits shall be risk differentiated, such that riskier obligors or large exposures are more frequent than less risky obligors of smaller exposures.

question: All legal documentation can be stored in a location of equivalent security and safety, not necessarily a bank vault.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 6.6.4 Documentation Lodging, Review and Follow-up) All legal documentation in respect of approved credit exposures shall be held in an appropriately secured bank vault or a location of equivalent security and safety.

question: The documentation and collateral need not agree with the approval document and customer agreement.
discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 6.6.4 Documentation Lodging, Review and Follow-up) Documentation and collateral must agree with that specified in the approval document as well as the agreement executed with the customer.

question: Existence and location of legal documentation shall be indicated in the credit file by an initialled receipt by the bank officer with responsibility for custody of such documentation.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 6.6.4 Documentation Lodging, Review and Follow-up) Existence and location of such legal documentation shall be indicated in the credit file by an initialled receipt by the bank officer with responsibility for custody of such documentation.

question: Credit files serve as the primary information source for decision-making on credits and customer relationships.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 6.7.1 File Management) The credit file serves as the primary information source for decision-making on credits and customer relationships.

question: Safe custody of credit files and maintaining records of file movement lies with
discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 6.7.1 File Management) Credit Risk Management shall be responsible for safe custody of credit files and maintaining records of file movement and use in and out of the file room.

question: What is the expected access level to credit files according to the provided information?

options.A: Accessible to anyone in the bank
options.B: Restricted to authorized officers of the bank

discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 6.7.1 File Management) Access to credit files shall be properly restricted to authorized officers of the bank.
community_answer: B. Restricted to authorized officers of the bank

question: All documentation generated during the credit cycle will be filed in the appropriate section of the credit file by Credit Risk Management.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 6.7.1 File Management) All documentation / correspondence generated during the credit cycle will be filed in the appropriate section of the credit file by the originating department.

question: Credit documents originating from the bank shall be domiciled on a Customer Credit Information Database accessible only to Credit Risk Management.
discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 6.7.1 File Management) All credit documents originating from the bank shall be (domiciled on a Customer Credit Information Database on the bank’s intranet), which shall be accessible to both credit risk management and relationship management function.

question: What is the purpose of credit portfolio planning?

options.A: Determine target markets and criteria for risk acceptance
options.B: Define the Bank's credit portfolio goals and objectives
options.C: Analyze and evaluate the current portfolio structure

discussion: Selected Answer: D. (Section 6.1 Credit Risk Portfolio Planning) Credit portfolio planning is the starting point of the Bank’s credit risk management process. It entails an analysis and evaluation of the current portfolio structure and a clear definition and agreement of the following: ➢ Target risk asset portfolio structure, broken down according to sector, product type, geographic regions, credit risk rating class, etc.; ➢ The Board-approved risk limits that the Bank is willing to permit relative to the Bank’s risk bearing capacity. ➢ The target markets and criteria for risk acceptance at the overall corporate level and across each risk creating business unit in the Bank. ➢ The Bank’s credit portfolio goals and objectives.

question: How often should the credit risk portfolio plan be approved by the Board?
discussion: Selected Answer: D. (Section 6.1 Credit Risk Portfolio Planning) The credit risk portfolio plan shall be prepared by Credit Portfolio Management and approved by the Board at the start of every financial year.

question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as an external factor in credit portfolio planning?
discussion: Selected Answer: C. (Section 6.1.2 Steps for carrying out credit portfolio planning) External factors include macroeconomic variables, global economic conditions, competition, inflation and political factors.

question: What factors influence Access Bank's portfolio concentration limits?
discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 6.1.3 Industry Selection and Prioritization) Our portfolio concentration limits will continue to be based on outlook and growth prospects, strategic importance of the industry and opportunities available to Access Bank.
community_answer: B. Industry outlook and growth prospects

question: What is the primary objective of Access Bank in optimizing its credit portfolio performance?
discussion: Selected Answer: C. (Section 6.1.3 Industry Selection and Prioritization) Access Bank will continuously employ techniques to optimize the performance of its credit portfolio with the objective of maximizing returns while minimizing risk.
community_answer: C. Maximizing returns while minimizing risk

question: Which of the following is mentioned as a sector that Access Bank intends to AVOID in its exposures?
discussion: Selected Answer: C. (Section 6.1.3 Industry Selection and Prioritization) We intend to AVOID exposures to Non-Target Market or high-risk names such as: Gambling.

question: Why are exposures to hazardous industries, like health-damaging or environmentally unfriendly businesses, intended to be avoided?

options.C: To protect the environment and public health

discussion: Selected Answer: C. (Section 6.1.3 Industry Selection and Prioritization) We aim to avoid areas that are harmful to the environment and do not form part of the bank’s target market.
community_answer: C. To protect the environment and public health

question: What are the two well-established techniques for expressing risk appetite in Access Bank?

options.A: Target market definition and Risk rejection criteria
options.B: Market segmentation and Credit program guidelines
options.C: Risk acceptance criteria and Industry profiles
options.D: Target market definition and Risk acceptance criteria

discussion: Selected Answer: D. (Section 6.1.4 Target Market and Risk Acceptance CriteriA) Two well established techniques for expressing risk appetite and which shall play critical roles in portfolio management in Access Bank are “Target market definition” and “Risk acceptance criteria”.
community_answer: D. Target market definition and Risk acceptance criteria

question: The use of unaudited financial statements for credit approval requests is encouraged.
discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 6.2.4.1 Unaudited Financial Statements) The use of unaudited financial statements for credit approval requests is discouraged.

question: Syndications involve situations where several banks come together to finance a given transaction due to its size or complexity
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 6.2.6 Syndications) Syndications are situations where several banks come together to finance a given transaction due to its size or complexity.

question: Is preliminary credit screening the responsibility of the relevant customer-facing market/relationship officer?
discussion: Selected Answer: A. (Section 6.2.1 Preliminary Credit Screening) Preliminary credit screening shall be the responsibility of the relevant customer-facing market/relationship officer and shall involve a largely high level and peripheral analysis of the acceptability of credit facility against credit criteria and facilitates early identification of unacceptable risk exposures and/or priority credits.

question: What is the role of the credit analyst in the credit risk evaluation process?
discussion: Selected Answer: C. (Section 6.2.4 Credit Risk Evaluation) Detailed credit analysis shall be conducted by credit analysts and documented on the Facility Approval Memorandum (FAM).

question: What is the primary document used to document the detailed credit analysis in the credit risk evaluation process?

options.A: Target Market / Risk Acceptance Criteria screen

discussion: Selected Answer: B. (Section 6.2.4 Credit Risk Evaluation) Detailed credit analysis shall be conducted by credit analysts and documented on the Facility Approval Memorandum (FAM).
